title: GSArch: Breaking Memory Barriers in 3D Gaussian Splatting Training via Architectural Support
problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) training is bottlenecked by three memory system inefficiencies: redundant off-chip DRAM loads for large 'hot' Gaussians accessed repeatedly across pixels, expensive atomic write operations during gradient accumulation, and severe bank conflicts during on-chip buffer reads during backward propagation.
method: GSArch introduces three architectural mechanisms targeting the three bottlenecks: (1) Hybrid memory management that classifies Gaussians as 'hot' (large, high pixel overlap, repeatedly loaded) or 'cold' and caches hot Gaussians in a fast on-chip buffer to eliminate redundant DRAM fetches; (2) Gradient informativeness filtering that identifies low-contribution gradients and skips their atomic write operations during backward propagation; (3) A rearrangement unit that packs conflicting on-chip memory read requests into non-conflicting bundles to eliminate bank conflicts. These techniques combine to accelerate the backward pass of 3DGS training.

title: Skia: Exposing Shadow Branches
problem: Modern processors using Fetch Directed Instruction Prefetching (FDIP) suffer from Branch Target Buffer (BTB) misses for instructions that have been previously decoded and evicted, causing the Branch Prediction Unit (BPU) to fail to recognize branches and either skip prefetching or speculate down wrong paths. These BTB misses stall the front-end and pollute the L1-I cache, a critical bottleneck for complex datacenter applications with large code footprints.
method: Skia introduces 'shadow branches': lightweight metadata structures that expose BTB-evicted branch information to the FDIP engine without restoring full BTB entries. When a branch is decoded and later evicted from the BTB, Skia retains shadow branch records (address and target hints) in a separate, higher-capacity structure. The FDIP engine consults these shadow records to continue speculative fetching along correct paths even when a BTB miss would otherwise halt prefetching or cause misdirection. This avoids both missed prefetches and wrong-path pollution of the L1-I cache.

title: H-Houdini: Scalable Invariant Learning
problem: Formal hardware verification via invariant learning (e.g., IC3/PDR) does not scale to large hardware designs because the invariant search space grows exponentially with state size, causing state-of-the-art tools to time out on real-world RTL designs.
method: H-Houdini extends the Houdini invariant-learning algorithm with scalability improvements targeting large hardware designs. The likely approach involves decomposing the hardware design into manageable sub-modules or abstract components, learning invariants compositionally (e.g., assume-guarantee or abstraction-refinement), and propagating learned invariants across the design hierarchy to avoid full-state enumeration. Specific algorithmic details are not disclosed in the available abstract.

title: Adyna: Accelerating Dynamic Neural Networks with Adaptive Scheduling
problem: Dynamic neural networks (DynNNs) conditionally skip computation based on input difficulty, but current GPUs and specialized accelerators lack dataflow and architecture support to realize the theoretical efficiency gains, because the dynamic execution patterns defeat static resource allocation.
method: Adyna uses a unified representation to model diverse DynNN variants and introduces a dynamism-aware multi-kernel selection paradigm. At runtime, a dataflow scheduler observes the distribution of dynamic size values (e.g., number of active tokens or blocks) and selects among multiple precompiled kernels, each optimized for a specific dynamic-size bucket. An effective kernel sampling algorithm chooses the minimal set of kernels to precompile and cache on the accelerator, balancing coverage against on-chip memory cost. The hardware architecture supports multi-tile and multi-tenant execution to handle concurrent dynamic workloads.

title: UniCAIM: A Unified CAM/CIM Architecture with Static-Dynamic KV Cache Pruning for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference
problem: Transformer LLM inference on long sequences suffers from massive KV cache memory and computation overhead; existing CIM accelerators support only static pruning with fixed patterns or inefficient dynamic pruning.
method: Proposes FeFET-based unified CAM/CIM architecture (UniCAIM) with three computation modes: 1) CAM mode for O(1) dynamic KV pruning via approximate similarity, 2) charge-domain CIM for static pruning with flexible patterns, 3) current-domain for exact attention on pruned KV. Leverages FeFET multi-level storage for signed multibit KV and in-place computation.

title: Resilient Federated Learning on Embedded Devices with Constrained Network Connectivity
problem: Federated learning deployment on resource-constrained embedded devices faces communication bottlenecks when network connectivity is limited; bandwidth-heavy gradient transmission prevents practical federated training.
method: Proposes adaptive federation framework where clients with limited bandwidth selectively transmit gradient updates. Uses gradient similarity score between local and global models to determine when compressed updates should be sent, adapting transmission strategy based on convergence state.

title: Quantum-Resistant Security: PQC Readiness and Research Challenges (Invited)
problem: Current classical cryptography protocols like RSA will be broken by cryptographically relevant quantum computers (CRQCs) within a few years, but implementation and adoption of post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards is difficult due to complexities in today's internet and computing stack.
method: The paper introduces Quartz (Quantum Risk and Threat Analyzer), a system for observability of quantum vulnerabilities in cryptography suites. The approach uses ciphersuite dependency graphs to map where quantum-unsafe cryptography is used and how it propagates through supply chains. Cryptography Bill of Materials (CBOM) generation provides visibility into risk exposure across systems.

title: Unlocking a New Rust Programming Experience: Fast and Slow Thinking with LLMs to Conquer Undefined Behaviors
problem: Eliminating Undefined Behaviors (UBs) in Rust programs written with the 'unsafe' tag; manual UB detection requires deep understanding of Rust safety rules and strong typing, which is laborious and error-prone.
method: RustBrain framework leveraging LLM semantic understanding with dual-process decision-making theory ('Fast and Slow Thinking'): (1) Fast thinking extracts features and generates solutions; (2) Slow thinking decomposes, verifies, and generalizes solutions abstractly. Feedback mechanism enables dynamic adjustment of verification and generalization results applied to solution generation.

title: StreamCSD: SSD-Autonomous Stream Management via In-Storage Content Learning
problem: Write amplification from garbage collection during SSD operation degrades performance and shortens lifespan; existing stream management solutions require host-side changes, hindering adoption.
method: StreamCSD uses compression ratios from embedded compressors in computational storage drives (CSDs) as a proxy for data compressibility. Applies streaming K-means to cluster data into streams based on compression similarity, enabling autonomous stream assignment without host involvement.

title: Composing Distributed Computations Through Task and Kernel Fusion
problem: Distributed task-based programs composed from multiple libraries incur significant overhead from redundant data movement and kernel launch costs when tasks from different libraries are executed separately, yet existing compilers and runtimes cannot see across library boundaries to fuse these tasks.
method: Diffuse introduces an intermediate representation (IR) for distributed computation that captures task graphs from multiple libraries in a unified form, enabling cross-boundary analysis. A JIT compiler then fuses compatible distributed tasks into single merged tasks, and further fuses the GPU kernels within those tasks using kernel fusion. The IR is general enough to represent computations from cuPyNumeric and Legate Sparse without modification to application code, and the JIT compilation is performed at runtime as task graphs become available.

title: 333-eDRAM - 3T Embedded DRAM Leveraging Monolithic 3D Integration of 3 Transistor Types: IGZO, Carbon Nanotube and Silicon FETs
problem: Embedded DRAM design faces fundamental trade-offs between high density, high retention time, high endurance, low access latency, low access energy, and low static leakage power. Traditional single-material DRAM cannot simultaneously optimize all of these dimensions.
method: 333-eDRAM uses monolithic 3D integration of three FET types: IGZO FETs (ultra-low leakage for high retention), Carbon Nanotube FETs (high drive current for fast access), and Silicon CMOS (efficient peripherals). The design co-optimizes all key metrics including EADP (energy-area-delay product) with full physical layout at 7nm. Evaluation includes cycle-accurate simulation and SPICE models calibrated to experimental data.

title: DIAS: Distance-based Attention Sparsity for Ultra-Long-Sequence Transformer with Tree-like Processing-in-Memory Architecture
problem: Transformer decode stage suffers from memory bandwidth bottleneck in attention and massive KV cache memory overhead; conventional attention sparsity methods degrade accuracy on ultra-long sequences (>1M tokens).
method: Distance-based irregular attention sparsity (DIAS) with approximate top-K attention (AKAttention) via graph-based search; tree-like PIM (TreePIM) architecture isolating KV cache into PIM units to improve both memory capacity and bandwidth.

title: MeshSlice: Efficient 2D Tensor Parallelism for Distributed DNN Training
problem: One-dimensional tensor parallelism (1D TP) for large DNN training scales poorly because all-reduce communication cost grows linearly with the number of devices. Existing 2D TP algorithms for general matrix multiplication (GeMM) have fundamental inefficiencies: Cannon's algorithm generates high traffic, SUMMA suffers from synchronization overhead, and 2D GeMM with standard collective communication operations cannot overlap communication with computation.
method: MeshSlice introduces a new 2D GeMM algorithm that decomposes collective communication operations into multiple smaller partial collectives, each of which can be issued and overlapped with ongoing matrix-multiply computation on the local shard. The algorithm maps the 2D device mesh such that partial all-reduces along one mesh dimension are issued while the other dimension is computing, hiding most communication latency behind arithmetic. An analytical autotuner searches over 2D mesh shape (rows x columns), GeMM dataflow configuration, and communication granularity (number of slices) to find the Pareto-optimal configuration for each LLM layer and cluster size, targeting TPUv4 hardware with its torus interconnect.

title: SAGA: A Memory-Efficient Accelerator for GANN Construction via Harnessing Vertex Similarity
problem: Graph-traversal-based Approximate Nearest Neighbor (GANN) construction faces severe memory bottlenecks due to high-dimensional vertices and dynamic graph updates. Existing accelerators like NDSearch struggle with the massive pre-processing overhead required for dynamic graph scenarios.
method: SAGA exploits vertex feature similarity by clustering vertices with the same starting point during the initial construction step. It decomposes vertices into key and non-key types with delta values in a narrow range, enabling mixed-precision quantization. A specialized two-level scheduling architecture with a bit-serial mixed-precision unit implements efficient GANN construction.

title: MAGE: A Multi-Agent Engine for Automated RTL Code Generation
problem: Single-LLM RTL generation approaches fail to produce syntactically and functionally correct Verilog due to the complexity of navigating multiple languages and handling generation, verification, and correction tasks simultaneously.
method: MAGE uses a multi-agent system with (1) high-temperature RTL candidate sampling that explores diverse candidate space, (2) Verilog-state checkpoint mechanism detecting functional errors early with precise feedback for targeted fixes, and (3) iterative debugging for improving candidate quality.

title: Scalable Community Detection Using Quantum Hamiltonian Descent and QUBO Formulation
problem: Community detection in large-scale graph data is computationally expensive with classical optimization; existing approaches lack scalability for diverse graph sizes and structures.
method: The approach reformulates community detection as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem and applies Quantum Hamiltonian Descent (QHD) to find optimal community structures. A multi-level algorithm iteratively refines community assignments by alternating between QUBO setup and QHD-based optimization.
